skill.name: creating-claude-agents
skill.description: Create and improve Claude Code agents with guidance for file structure, frontmatter, persona design, tool access, model selection, examples, and schema validation.
skill.summary: Guides creation and review of Claude Code agent files with schema-aware best practices.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline formatting, schema examples, and documentation links. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found. The remaining risks are overbroad tool-permission examples and an author-specific local path disclosure.

remediation.suggestion: Make restricted tools the default in examples. Avoid recommending inherited all-tool access unless the user explicitly accepts the risk.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted Bash in full development example
remediation.suggestion: Replace unrestricted Bash with specific patterns such as Bash(git *) or task-specific commands. Explain when broader Bash needs separate approval.
Remove the absolute local path or replace it with a repository-relative path that users can adapt.

static_findings.snippet: Agents must be placed in `.claude/agents/` directory as markdown files.
| `description` | string | Brief overview of functionality and use cases | `Reviews code for best pr
| `allowed-tools` | string | Comma-separated list of available tools | `Read, Write, Bash, WebSearch
| `agentType` | string | Explicit marker for format preservation | `agent` |
| Missing required field 'name' | Frontmatter lacks name field | Add `name: agent-name` |
| Missing required field 'description' | Frontmatter lacks description | Add `description: ...` |
| Invalid model value | Model not in enum | Use: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, or `inherit` |
| Missing H1 heading | Content doesn't start with # | Add `# Agent Name` as first line |
Omit the `allowed-tools` field to inherit all tools from the parent conversation:
| Using `_` in name | Violates pattern constraint | Use hyphens: `code-reviewer` not `code_reviewer`
| Uppercase in name | Violates pattern constraint | Lowercase only: `debugger` not `Debugger` |
| No H1 heading | Content format invalid | Start content with `# Agent Name` |
| No agentType field | May lose type info in conversion | Add `agentType: agent` |
- `code-reviewer` - Reviews code for quality and security
- `debugger` - Root cause analysis and minimal fixes
- `code-helper` - Reviews, debugs, tests, refactors, documents (too broad)

content.value_statement: Creating reliable Claude Code agents requires correct frontmatter, tool limits, and clear personas. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through agent structure, validation, and review.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required .claude/agents/*.md file location and Markdown structure.
Defines required and optional frontmatter fields for Claude Code agents.
Provides examples for personas, process sections, and output formats.
Guides model selection across sonnet, opus, haiku, and inherit modes.
Shows tool access patterns, including restricted Bash examples.
Lists validation checks and common agent authoring mistakes.
limitations: It is reference guidance, not an automatic validator or installer.
Some examples use broad tool permissions and need careful review.
Schema URLs may change, so users should verify current Claude Code documentation.
It focuses on Claude Code agents, not general chatbot deployment.

use_cases.title: Create a New Agent
use_cases.description: Draft a Claude Code agent with valid frontmatter, a focused persona, and a clear process.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Permissions
use_cases.description: Check whether an agent uses minimal tools and safer Bash restrictions before sharing it with a team.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Agent Patterns
use_cases.description: Use consistent naming, model choices, examples, and validation checks across many repository agents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code agent for reviewing documentation changes. Include a focused name, description, persona, tools, model choice, and validation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Claude Code agent and improve its activation description, persona, process steps, examples, and tool permissions while preserving its purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Agent Tool Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this agent for excessive tool access. Recommend safer allowed-tools settings and explain any tradeoffs for Bash, Write, WebSearch, and WebFetch.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a small set of specialized Claude Code agents for code review, debugging, testing, and documentation. Avoid overlapping responsibilities and define validation rules.

output_examples.input: Create a read-only code review agent.
output: A focused agent name and activation description.
A reviewer persona with quality and security priorities.
A minimal tool set centered on reading and searching files.
A short review process with file-specific feedback expectations.

output_examples.input: Improve this broad code helper agent.
output: A recommendation to split broad responsibilities into specialized agents.
Clearer activation language for each proposed agent.
Safer tool permissions for read-only and edit-capable tasks.
Validation checks for naming, description length, and model values.

output_examples.input: Audit an agent that uses Write and unrestricted Bash.
output: A risk summary for broad file and command access.
Suggested restricted Bash patterns for expected workflows.
A note to require explicit approval before granting full development permissions.

best_practices: Keep each agent focused on one measurable responsibility.
Use the smallest tool set that supports the agent workflow.
Validate frontmatter, naming, model values, and content structure before sharing agents.
anti_patterns: Creating one broad agent for reviewing, debugging, testing, and documentation.
Granting unrestricted Bash or inherited tools when read-only access is enough.
Using vague activation descriptions that do not state when the agent should run.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code agent Markdown files with valid frontmatter, personas, process steps, examples, and tool settings.

faq.question: Does it install agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides authoring guidance. The host environment must create, edit, or validate files.

faq.question: Can it help with agent validation errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common validation failures for names, descriptions, model values, headings, and required fields.

faq.question: How should I choose a model?
faq.answer: Use sonnet for most agents, opus for deep reasoning, haiku for simple checks, and inherit when parent context should decide.

faq.question: Are broad tool permissions safe?
faq.answer: Broad permissions increase risk. Start with minimal tools and restrict Bash commands to expected workflows when possible.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill content?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful for Codex, Claude, and Claude Code users who author Claude Code agent files.
